answer: T-Levels are a two-year technical qualification for students aged 16 to 19. They combine classroom learning with a substantial industry placement, so students can develop practical skills and understand how their learning applies in the workplace.

T-Levels and A-Levels are different routes. A-Levels are generally more academic and are often chosen by students planning to go to university, while T-Levels are more technical and career-focused, with work placement experience built into the qualification.

T-Levels are usually a strong fit for students who enjoy practical learning, want hands-on experience, and are interested in a specific technical field such as digital, construction, engineering, health, or education. They can suit students who prefer applied learning over a purely academic route.

A key feature of T-Levels is the industry placement. Students spend time with an employer in a real working environment, so they can apply theory in practice, build confidence, and learn workplace expectations.

T-Levels can lead to employment, apprenticeships, higher-level technical study, or university depending on the subject and the student's next steps. They are designed to provide both practical experience and a strong foundation for progression.

T-Levels are useful for students who want a more applied route than traditional A-Levels. They offer subject-specific learning, industry experience, and a direct connection to work, which can make students more prepared for technical roles or further training.

T-Levels are Level 3 qualifications, which sit broadly in line with A-Levels in the education system. They are designed to be a valued alternative route, especially for students interested in technical and applied work.

Ada College is a specialist digital and technology college, and a T-Level pathway can be especially relevant for students interested in digital careers, creative technology, software, data, and technical roles. The route can be a strong match for learners who want practical, employer-facing education in digital sectors.
